summary: Jordan issues most nationalities a single-entry visa on arrival for JOD 40 allowing a 30-day stay, and waives that fee entirely for travellers who buy the Jordan Pass (which bundles Petra and 40+ sites) and stay at least three nights — while a handful of nationalities still need prior approval or an embassy visa.

conditionalWaivers.text: Foreign nationals residing in GCC countries with residence valid for at least 6 months can obtain a visa on arrival in Jordan (nationals of the Philippines and Nigeria still need pre-approval).

source.name: Visit Jordan — visas and entry information

fee.notes: Payable in Jordanian dinars (cards accepted at Amman airport). Double-entry (JOD 60) and multiple-entry (JOD 120) visas are available from embassies. The fee is waived for Jordan Pass holders staying at least 3 nights, and for travellers arriving via Aqaba's special economic zone.

source.name: Visit Jordan — visas and entry information

passportValidity.text: Your passport must be valid for at least 6 months on the date of arrival in Jordan.

vaccinations.name: Yellow fever
vaccinations.text: A yellow fever vaccination certificate is required only for travellers arriving from countries with risk of yellow fever transmission.

travelInsurance.text: Travel insurance is not an entry requirement, but medical cover is strongly recommended — private hospitals in Amman are good but charge foreigners for treatment.

onwardTicket.text: Airlines and border officers may ask for proof of onward or return travel within your permitted stay.

proofOfFunds.text: No fixed amount is published; border officers may ask visitors to show sufficient means for their stay.

currencyLimits.text: Cash worth JOD 15,000 or more (or the foreign-currency equivalent) must be declared on arrival and departure.

source.name: Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Expatriates of Jordan

notes: Duty-free allowance: 200 cigarettes and 1 litre of alcohol per adult.
Drones require prior authorisation and are routinely confiscated at the border without it.

payments.text: Cards are accepted in Amman hotels, malls and larger restaurants, but Petra-area shops, taxis and rural Jordan run on cash. Note that the dinar is a high-value currency (1 JOD is roughly 1.4 USD) — small notes are useful for tips and taxis.

safety.text: Jordan is one of the region's most stable and welcoming countries and tourist areas are generally safe. Exercise normal precautions, avoid the immediate Syria and Iraq border areas, and follow local news given wider regional tensions.

source.name: U.S. Department of State — Jordan Travel Advisory

bestTimeToVisit.text: Spring (March–May) and autumn (September–November) offer mild weather ideal for Petra, Wadi Rum and the Dead Sea; summers are very hot and winters can be surprisingly cold, with occasional snow in Amman.

tips.text: Buy the Jordan Pass (jordanpass.jo) before arrival if you will stay at least 3 nights: from JOD 70 it waives the JOD 40 visa fee and includes Petra (normally JOD 50 alone) plus 40+ other sites — it pays for itself on Petra and the visa alone.

Enter Petra at opening time (6 am) — you will walk the Siq to the Treasury in cool air and beat both the crowds and the midday heat; wear proper walking shoes, the site is far bigger than most visitors expect.
At the Dead Sea, float on your back and keep the water away from your eyes and any cuts — shower promptly afterwards, and bring flip-flops as the salt crystals are sharp.
Do not drink tap water in Jordan — the country is one of the most water-scarce on earth and supply is intermittent; stick to bottled or filtered water.

faq.question: Do US citizens need a visa for Jordan?
faq.answer: Yes, but it is issued on arrival: a single-entry visa costs JOD 40 (about USD 56) and allows a 30-day stay, extendable in-country to a total of about 3 months. Buy a Jordan Pass before travel and stay at least 3 nights and the visa fee is waived entirely.

faq.question: Is the Jordan Pass worth it?
faq.answer: Almost always, if you stay at least 3 nights and visit Petra. The cheapest pass (JOD 70) already covers the JOD 40 visa fee plus one-day Petra entry (JOD 50 bought separately) — more than paying for itself — and adds Wadi Rum, Jerash and 40+ other sites. Buy it online at jordanpass.jo before you arrive.

faq.question: How do I pay for the Jordan visa on arrival?
faq.answer: The JOD 40 fee is charged in Jordanian dinars. At Queen Alia International Airport you can pay by card or exchange money before the immigration counters; at land borders bring cash. Jordan Pass holders skip payment and simply show the pass QR code.

faq.question: Can I stay in Jordan longer than 30 days?
faq.answer: Yes. Register at a local police station before your initial 30 days expire and your stay can be extended to a total of about 3 months without leaving the country. Overstaying without registering incurs a fine of JOD 1.5 per day at departure.

faq.question: Can Indian citizens get a visa on arrival in Jordan?
faq.answer: Generally yes — Indian passport holders have been able to obtain the JOD 40 visa on arrival, but conditions for Indian, Filipino, Indonesian and Vietnamese nationals have changed several times (group-travel or prior-approval requirements have applied in some periods). Confirm the current rule with a Jordanian embassy or your airline before booking.
